boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations in Rockhurst’s surrounding 49/63 orbit, each anchored to a nearby corridor.

cards.entity_name: Anita B. Gorman Conservation Discovery Center
cards.title: Native trails on Troost
cards.subtitle: Troost Avenue corridor — 4750 Troost Ave.
cards.notes: Start with the short trails and native-plant areas, then look through the indoor nature exhibits during building hours.
cards.short_summary: A conservation center with trails, exhibits, and regular nature programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Missouri Department of Conservation describes eight acres of natural areas, trails, native-plant beds, indoor exhibits, and free nature programs at the center.
cards.source_title: The Anita B. Gorman Conservation Discovery Center
cards.access_notes: Grounds are open daily during daylight hours; check the official page for building hours and holiday closures.

cards.entity_name: Ewing and Muriel Kauffman Memorial Garden
cards.title: Sculpture and plantings on Rockhill
cards.subtitle: Rockhill Road corridor — 4801 Rockhill Road
cards.notes: Walk the brick paths, look for Tom Corbin’s bronze sculptures, and use personal snapshots rather than a portrait session.
cards.short_summary: A public garden pairing seasonal displays, fountains, and bronze sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: Kauffman Foundation says admission and parking are free and describes bronze sculptures, fountains, and changing annual displays.
cards.source_title: Ewing and Muriel Kauffman Memorial Garden
cards.access_notes: Open to all ages; the garden prohibits alcohol, biking, dogs except service animals, and portrait photography.

cards.title: Science collections on Cherry
cards.subtitle: Cherry Street corridor — 5109 Cherry Street
cards.notes: Browse the public science library and arboretum; plan around regular hours before making the short trip from campus.
cards.short_summary: A public science library set on an arboretum grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: Linda Hall Library states that it is open to the public free of charge, lists its address, and posts regular library hours.
cards.source_title: The Linda Hall: Science Library and Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Regular hours listed are Monday–Friday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and the second Saturday 10 a.m.–2 p.m.; confirm before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Plaza Branch, Kansas City Public Library
cards.title: Books and Brush Creek on Main
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 4801 Main Street
cards.notes: Use a study pod or browse, then step to the windows for the library’s documented view over Brush Creek.
cards.short_summary: A public branch with study pods, youth resources, and an auditorium.
cards.evidence_claim: Kansas City Public Library lists Plaza Branch at 4801 Main Street and identifies study pods, Wi-Fi, youth resources, and windows overlooking Brush Creek.
cards.source_title: Plaza Branch | Kansas City Public Library
cards.access_notes: The official location page posts hours and notes free parking in the branch garage.

cards.title: Collection time on Oak
cards.subtitle: Oak Street corridor — 4525 Oak Street
cards.notes: Choose a gallery route before you go, then leave time to look through works across the museum’s collection.
cards.short_summary: A major art museum whose general admission is free for everyone.
cards.evidence_claim: Nelson-Atkins states that member support keeps general admission free for everyone and lists the museum at 4525 Oak Street.
cards.access_notes: General admission is free; special exhibitions, programs, and parking may have separate terms.

cards.title: Volker Fountain on Oak
cards.subtitle: Oak Street corridor — 4701 Oak Street
cards.notes: Walk through the park and pause at the William Volker Memorial Fountain, then continue along the cultural corridor.
cards.short_summary: A 13.81-acre park with the William Volker Memorial Fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: Kansas City Parks lists Theis Park at 4701 Oak Street, identifies the Volker Memorial Fountain, and notes it is across from the Nelson-Atkins Museum.
cards.access_notes: Kansas City Parks lists daily hours of 5 a.m.–midnight.

cards.title: Current work on Warwick
cards.subtitle: Warwick Boulevard corridor — 4415 Warwick Blvd.
cards.notes: Check the exhibition listing, then visit during public gallery hours or arrange an appointment for another day.
cards.short_summary: Kansas City Art Institute’s public-facing gallery space.
cards.evidence_claim: KCAI states that its gallery at 4415 Warwick Boulevard is open to the public and posts Wednesday–Sunday visitor hours.
cards.access_notes: Public hours are Wednesday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m.; other visits are by appointment.

cards.entity_name: The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures
cards.title: Tiny worlds on Oak
cards.subtitle: Oak Street corridor — 5235 Oak Street
cards.notes: Reserve ahead if needed and focus on a gallery section; the museum also schedules free-admission Second Sundays.
cards.short_summary: A museum of historically significant toys and fine-scale miniatures.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum’s visitor page lists 5235 Oak Street, recommends advance ticket reservations, and states that every second Sunday has free admission.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures
cards.access_notes: Admission tickets are generally sold; free admission is offered every second Sunday. Museum parking is free.

cards.title: A map stop on Troost
cards.subtitle: Troost Avenue corridor — 4825 Troost
cards.notes: Use UMKC’s campus map to orient yourself to the neighboring Volker campus and its listed Troost building.
cards.short_summary: A named UMKC Volker Campus building on the Troost corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC’s registrar lists the 4825 Troost Building as a Volker Campus building location.
cards.access_notes: This is an active university building; observe campus access and visitor rules.

cards.title: Contemporary art on Warwick
cards.subtitle: Warwick Boulevard corridor — 4420 Warwick Boulevard
cards.notes: Check the museum’s current exhibition and public-program listings before setting out, since special events can change access.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art museum destination on the Warwick cultural corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Kemper Museum’s official gala page identifies the museum’s address as 4420 Warwick Boulevard in Kansas City.
cards.source_title: Kemper Museum Gala — Know Before You Go
cards.access_notes: Confirm gallery access and any event-specific requirements directly with the museum before visiting.
